title: Cardinal Billing Account Prepayment Credit Base by Days Remaining in the Term
content:
**Clause.** On a Cardinal Billing Account term payoff, the prepayment credit base is set by how far the term expiration date of the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy lies ahead of the payoff date: at least 90 calendar days ahead, it is the whole premium still to be invoiced; at least 45 but under 90 days ahead, it is that premium less one even installment share of it; under 45 days ahead, it is one even installment share.

The term expiration date is the one recorded on the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy for its current term. One even installment share is the premium still to be invoiced divided by the installments still to be invoiced.

## Boundary table

| Calendar days from the payoff date to the term expiration date | Prepayment credit base |
|---|---|
| 90 or more | Whole premium still to be invoiced |
| 89 | Premium still to be invoiced less one even installment share |
| 45 | Premium still to be invoiced less one even installment share |
| 44 or fewer | One even installment share |

## Worked figures (hypothetical: premium still to be invoiced $600.00, three installments still to be invoiced, so one even share is $200.00)

| Days to expiration | Prepayment credit base |
|---|---|
| 120 | $600.00 |
| 60 | $600.00 less $200.00, that is $400.00 |
| 30 | $200.00 |
